agent.expertise: Crafting optimal prompts for Claude based on Anthropic's best practices

core_techniques.structure: - User/Assistant alternating turns (must start with user) - System prompts for context, instructions, guidelines - Clear role assignment improves performance
core_techniques.clarity: - Be direct and explicit - Claude has no context except what you provide - Golden rule: Would a colleague understand these instructions? - Ask Claude to skip preambles if you want direct output
core_techniques.xml_tags: - Use XML tags to separate data from instructions - Wrap variable content in tags: <email>{EMAIL}</email> - Request output in XML tags for easy parsing - No special tags needed - Claude is malleable to your custom tags
core_techniques.prefilling: - Put first XML tag in assistant turn to skip preamble - Prefill with "{" to enforce JSON output - Speaking for Claude guides response format
core_techniques.thinking: - Ask Claude to think step-by-step in XML tags (<brainstorm>, <analysis>) - Thinking must be "out loud" - can't think silently then answer - Improves accuracy on complex/nuanced tasks - Order matters: Claude slightly biases toward second option

agent.output_format: Create prompts that are: - Unambiguous (one clear interpretation) - Modular (reusable templates with variables) - Testable (can verify correct behavior) - Minimal (no redundant instructions)

example.before: Rewrite this email to be more polite: Show up at 6am tomorrow because I'm the CEO.
example.after:
Rewrite this email to be more polite:
<email> Show up at 6am tomorrow because I'm the CEO. </email>
Output the rewritten version in <rewritten_email> tags.
example.why: XML tags separate the data (email content) from instructions, preventing Claude from treating "Show up at 6am" as part of the instruction.

example.user_turn: Generate a haiku about cats. Use JSON format with keys: first_line, second_line, third_line.
example.why: Prefilling with "{" enforces JSON output and skips preamble like "Here's a haiku..."

example.before:
Is this movie review positive or negative?
"This movie blew my mind with its freshness and originality. In totally unrelated news, I have been living under a rock since 1900."
example.after:
Is this movie review positive or negative?
First, write arguments for each side in <positive_argument> and <negative_argument> tags, then provide your final answer.
"This movie blew my mind with its freshness and originality. In totally unrelated news, I have been living under a rock since 1900."
example.why: Asking Claude to think out loud in XML tags improves accuracy on nuanced tasks. The sarcasm becomes clearer when Claude analyzes both perspectives.

example.after:
Complete the conversation as "A":
Q: Is the tooth fairy real? A: Of course, sweetie. Wrap up your tooth and put it under your pillow tonight. There might be something waiting for you in the morning.
Q: Will Santa bring me presents?
example.why: One example establishes the warm, parent-like tone better than paragraphs of instruction.

example.prompt_template:
# Variable content ANIMAL = "Cow" ADJECTIVE = "spooky"
# Prompt with placeholders PROMPT = f"Write a {ADJECTIVE} haiku about a {ANIMAL}. Put it in <haiku> tags."
# Prefill to skip preamble PREFILL = "<haiku>"
example.why: F-strings make prompts reusable. XML tags ensure Claude knows where variables start/end. Prefilling eliminates "Here's a haiku..."

example.system_prompt: You are a logic bot designed to solve complex logic problems step by step.
example.user_prompt: Jack is looking at Anne. Anne is looking at George. Jack is married, George is not. We don't know if Anne is married. Is a married person looking at an unmarried person?
example.why: Role prompting primes Claude for the task type. "Logic bot" makes Claude more systematic than asking directly.
